nieuwmarkt: The Zeedijk, the street of Chinese restaurants and temples, Nieuwmarkt square with the Waag (the 17th-century weigh house) and, a little further on, the Oude Kerk, the city's oldest church, in the middle of the red-light district lanes.
dam: Dam Square, Royal Palace and Nieuwe Kerk
The historic heart of Amsterdam: the square with the National Monument, the Royal Palace (once the town hall), the Nieuwe Kerk next door and, behind it, the maze of shopping streets.
spui: Begijnhof, Spui and the flower market

The Begijnhof, a hidden 14th-century courtyard with the city's oldest wooden house and a quiet garden; then Spui square with its bookshops and the Bloemenmarkt, the flower market floating on the Singel canal.
canali: Amsterdam's loveliest walk: along Herengracht, Keizersgracht and Prinsengracht, narrow gabled houses and bridges. The Nine Streets have small shops and cafés, and at the end is the Westerkerk, with the city's tallest tower. In front is the Anne Frank House, to see from outside.
jordaan: The most romantic neighbourhood: lanes of low houses, hofjes (hidden courtyards), galleries and local cafés, up to the Noordermarkt and Brouwersgracht, the most photographed canal.
museumplein: The great lawn with the Rijksmuseum at one end, the Van Gogh Museum and the Concertgebouw on the sides, surrounded by 19th-century villas. Under the Rijksmuseum runs a cycle tunnel that is one of the most photographed shortcuts.
pijp: De Pijp and the Albert Cuyp market
The city's liveliest and most multicultural neighbourhood: the Albert Cuyp market with cheese, stroopwafels and herring, cafés under the plane trees and Sarphatipark, a quiet park nearby.
annefrankins: The secret annexe where Anne Frank and her family hid for two years: the revolving bookcase, the empty rooms and her original diaries. A short but intense visit.
rijks: The Dutch national museum: Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer, the 17th-century masters, the model ships and the Cuypers Library. Three hours are enough for the masterpieces.
vangogh: The world's largest collection of Vincent van Gogh: the Sunflowers, the Potato Eaters and the development of his painting from his Dutch beginnings to the works from Arles.
jodenbuurt: The former Jewish quarter: the Waterlooplein flea market, the Stopera opera house on the Amstel, Rembrandt's house from outside, the Portuguese Synagogue and, further on, the Plantage with the botanical garden and Artis zoo.
vondel: The locals' favourite park, with ponds, lawns and green parakeets in the trees. In Oud-West, ten minutes away, the old tram depot houses the Foodhallen, a big indoor market of food from around the world.
noord: Free ferry to Amsterdam Noord and EYE

Free GVB ferries leave from behind Central Station: in 5 minutes you reach Noord, where the futuristic EYE building (the film museum) has a café with a terrace on the IJ river and a view of the skyline.
